answer: Each new key commits a pigment: a salted MinHash of its recent counterparties and inter-arrival times. Admission opens only in a short tide window after the epoch seed is published. The ledger then computes the pairwise Jaccard delta of new pigments versus each other and versus already-weighted identities. Keys whose delta falls below a tight threshold collapse into one cluster that shares a single vote, reward share, and slashable reserve. A factory minting lookalike accounts cannot multiply influence in the same tide; an isolated pigment far from every cluster accrues weight alone.
